gloss: to grow accustomed through practice; to get used to doing

definitions.gloss: to grow accustomed to (something) through repeated learning or practice
definitions.explanation: A compound verb combining {習|なら}う (to learn) with {慣|な}れる (to get used to). Describes reaching a state where a skill or routine feels natural after enough practice.

examples.japanese: {習|なら}い{慣|な}れた{道|みち}を{通|とお}る。
examples.english: I take a route I'm used to.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}{使|つか}っているので、{操作|そうさ}にもう{習|なら}い{慣|な}れた。
examples.english: I use it every day, so I've gotten used to operating it.

examples.japanese: {敬語|けいご}は{習|なら}い{慣|な}れるまでに{時間|じかん}がかかるが、{自然|しぜん}に{出|で}てくるようになる。
examples.english: Keigo takes time to get used to, but eventually it comes out naturally.

notes:
Compound of {習|なら}う (to learn) + {慣|な}れる (to grow accustomed). Conjugates as an ichidan verb like {慣|な}れる. The literary register is mild — common in writing about skills, languages, and work routines.

USAGE:
- Past form most common: {習|なら}い{慣|な}れた is used attributively ({習|なら}い{慣|な}れた{道|みち}, {習|なら}い{慣|な}れた{仕事|しごと}).
- Predicative {習|なら}い{慣|な}れる appears in writing about gradually mastering something.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {慣|な}れる: to get used to — broader and more common; covers any kind of habituation
- {身|み}に{付|つ}く: to be acquired (as a skill) — focuses on the skill becoming a permanent part of oneself
- {使|つか}い{慣|な}れる: to get used to using something — parallel compound for tools or systems
